method: QUOTED UNDER A 200-WORD BUDGET (197 words used), from Cancer Council Australia 'COSA guidelines for the nutritional management of adult patients with head and neck cancer' v1.3 (published 2025-08-22), retrieved 2026-09-23 as MAGICapp JSON. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read, NOT openly licensed. Cancer Council Australia's guideline FAQ: fair dealing needs only correct citation; reproducing 'more than 200 words or figures/tables' needs permission from guidelines@cancer.org.au. So quotes here are capped at 200 words per source guideline (enforced by the generator) and tables were stripped from the retrieved text before quoting, so none can be quoted.

claims.claim: **Dietitian review weekly during (chemo)radiotherapy, then at minimum fortnightly for at least 6 weeks after treatment.**
claims.source_text: We recommend patients are reviewed weekly by a dietitian during (chemo)radiotherapy for HNC, and at minimum fortnightly for at least 6 weeks post treatment.
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'COSA guidelines for the nutritional management of adult patients with head and neck cancer', v1.3, published 2025-08-22, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/Eez3Kj, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After that, dietitian review as clinically indicated, for as long as malnutrition, weight loss, chronic toxicities or tube feeding need managing.**
claims.source_text: reviewed by a dietitian as clinically indicated, for as long they require management of malnutrition, weight loss, chronic toxicities, and/or tube feeding

claims.claim: **Prophylactic versus reactive nutrition support:** decide with dietitians, other clinicians, patients and caregivers. There may be little to no difference in long-term outcomes, **but the prophylactic approach improves short-term quality of life.**
claims.source_text: We recommend consultation between dietitians and other multidisciplinary clinicians, patients and caregivers … There may be little to no difference between prophylactic or reactive nutrition support on long-term nutrition and clinical outcomes. … the prophylactic approach does demonstrate improved short-term quality of life outcomes
